publicationStmt.p: Amores Project working trial. Prepared for editorial review, 8 September 2026; not an approved critical edition.

handDesc.handNote: The principal text is written in brown ink. Darker interventions occur between lines, on the baseline and in the margins. They are not assigned to a single historical correcting hand in this trial.

origin.p: The supplied library IIIF metadata dates the manuscript to the 10th/11th century. This is catalogue information; it does not date individual interventions.

surrogates.p: Digital facsimile: Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin, PPN1844735508. The supplied manifest marks the images Public Domain Mark 1.0. Folios 63r, 63v and 64r were inspected at enlarged resolution for this trial.

projectDesc.p: Trial based on all 84 verse lines in the three source images and the project's existing manuscript commentary. Supersedes the earlier 86-line example. Observations and unresolved interpretations are distinguished in the review notes. Transcription and review responsibility are not claims of scholarly approval.

correction.p: No modern edition is silently substituted for the witness. Uncertain characters use unclear; tentative interventions use cert. Darker ink alone uses hi, not an assertion of erasure or a newly identified hand. Underlying text that cannot be securely read is not reconstructed.

normalization.p: The single manuscript display preserves spellings and selected visible signs; long s and ordinary letter allographs are generally represented by standard Latin letters. Word spacing is editorially segmented and is not a measurement of the original. Expansions are retained in the TEI as explicit alternatives for analysis, not as a second reader view. No normalized critical text is supplied. Curled abbreviation signs, the crossed q in qd, and marginal punctuation are typographic approximations.

punctuation.p: Visible significant punctuation and word-division marks are recorded. Question-like signs are represented schematically by ⸮. No systematic modern punctuation has been added.

segmentation.p: Each l corresponds to one verse and one physical manuscript line in this passage. Groups represent elegiac couplets; even-line indentation follows the visible source layout. Each line points to a facsimile zone derived from the existing manually authored annotation rectangle. Main-text zones do not necessarily enclose marginal additions.

interpretation.p: Every first-pass note and all 84 lines received an independent second-agent image review. Notes of type observation record supported readings or settled encoding policy. Notes of type uncertainty document limits of the image or the transcription without requiring a reader decision. Only type review identifies consequential unresolved interventions for editorial attention. The lower-margin inscription on 63v is retained as an unexpanded uncertain annotation. Marginal annotations are not silently inserted into the verse. This second pass is not human editorial approval.

revisionDesc.change: Reworked the complete 3.7Y trial against all three folios; restored 84-line sequence, declared display policy and image links, and recorded unresolved readings for human review.

Independently compared all 84 lines and all first-pass notes with enlarged facsimiles of 63r, 63v and 64r. Replaced four conjectural erasures with low-certainty faint readings; corrected the qd sign placement; restricted the uncertain marginal reading at 51; distinguished documented uncertainties from three unresolved editorial interventions. No human approval is implied.

Renewed source-image inspection of verses 10, 51, 55. Retained conservative unclear/gap and intervention markup; reassessed the remaining questions as documented image uncertainty under the current workflow. No complete reading or correction sequence is inferred, and no human approval is implied.

item.note: The three small v additions at 1–2 turn at into aut. The barred e above formonsa is expanded as est in the TEI. The placements and signs are supported by 63r; their shapes are approximated typographically.
Supralinear le follows ma; a small mark below draws attention to the insertion. The insertion point and the separate lower mark are visible on 63r.

A faint trace between crimen and onusque is retained as a low-certainty n. The image does not securely establish either the letter or a deletion action. The earlier erasure markup has therefore been removed.

A faint c-like trace is visible between effe and ti. It is retained as a low-certainty reading with reason faded; the image does not establish the mechanism that made it faint. No deletion action is asserted.
The t in sit is marked below and crossed through. The remaining thonica is retained; the spelling is not silently corrected to Sithonia.

The small supralinear q with a curled suspension sign is visible after Oscula. The display qꝫ and TEI expansion que follow the declared abbreviation policy; exact imitation of the pen shape is not an unresolved reading.

The u above Lascium and t in posuique are visible on 63r. The separate supralinear cluster before posuique remains tentatively read sup, without a secure expansion or identifiable function. It is retained as a low-certainty unclear addition. Its possible abbreviation or annotation function is documented as uncertainty; no choice between unsupported interpretations is needed for this source transcription.

Mihi is legible in darker writing on a disturbed area. The underlying sequence cannot be securely recovered from this image, so no earlier nihil is reconstructed. The current reading is supported; the earlier state remains unknown.
The final e of Etque has a descending tail, represented by ę. The TEI records ae as its regularized alternative. Preterea remains unnormalized.
The g of gelida is legible in darker ink. An underlying c cannot be securely recovered. The transcription records the visible g and does not invent an earlier reading.
The beginning of propositum is darker and includes a barred p, expanded as pro in the TEI. The earlier state beneath this writing is not legible enough to reconstruct.
A small vertical word-division mark separates iners and iacui. It is recorded independently of the editorial word spacing.
A supralinear barred e after exactum is visible and expanded as est in the TEI.

The final supralinear que sign and the undercurve joining pud to the et sign are visible. The h-like trace after A remains a low-certainty reading. The transcription does not identify a historical correcting hand or impose modern word division.
Flaua, chlide, and ter are close together. Word spacing is editorially segmented; the small diacritics in chlide are approximated by ï. Names retain the witness capitalization.

An irregular dark stroke is visible between sustinuisse and nouem. Its function and any earlier text beneath it cannot be established from this image. It is retained as an unknown-function mark, with no erased letters supplied.

The enlarged opening shows Nun: the final character has the two-minim form of n, unlike the three-minim m in the nearby num in line 28. Nun is retained as a witness reading, without grammatical emendation.

The visible carmen has darker m and final n. A proposed earlier carnem is not securely legible and is not reconstructed. The right marginal sign is displayed schematically as ⸮ under the declared punctuation policy.
Phoenicea is supported by 63v. The earlier example’s undeclared apostrophe glyph has no secure counterpart here and remains excluded.

The ie of iecur is darker, beside faint traces tentatively represented by g. The g remains low-certainty; the earlier erasure assertion has been replaced by neutral faded-reading markup. No earlier word is reconstructed.
The image supports Carminae lesa and uanescit. The earlier example’s uescit is unsupported. Witness spellings and the small separating stop are retained.
A faint vertical trace between ner and uos is retained as a low-certainty long s. Its identity and physical history cannot be established; the earlier erasure assertion has been removed.

The right margin shows i and a barred n, displayed as in̄. Its expansion and relation to the verse remain unknown. Keeping the annotation unexpanded and outside the verse reading is the settled policy for this image.
Mei is legible in darker ink. The image does not establish a prior reading beneath it, and none is reconstructed.

The visible baseline supports qualem tetigique. The darker t, the suspension in qualē, and the darker qualem tetigi are recorded. No marginal e is visible at the asserted location; a proposed underlying cecidi cannot be recovered securely.

The small mark above the y-like letter is displayed as ẏ. The adjoining sequence is retained as ad tactu, with editorial word spacing. The exact allograph and the crowded boundary after ad remain image-level uncertainties; no unattested final m is supplied.
The e in ille is marked below and i is added above it. The TEI substitution records both visible states without replacing the witness with a silently corrected word.

Nunc is clearly written above the caret after Quas. Onci in concipiam is darker, with a visible division and earlier traces beneath it. The present intervention is recorded; the earlier letters are not securely recoverable.

The crowded opening remains a low-certainty Credoe. The enlarged image supports an extra e-like form after the rounded letter but does not securely establish whether it is a separate letter or reworking. Word-division marks and darker tur are visible and retained. No normalizing Credo is imposed.
The separating stops after ferre, tuli and esse are recorded once each. The image does not support the duplicated punctuation in the previous example.

The darker e after fortuna, the suspension in tantūm, and darker dona si and final u are visible. The qd sign crosses the descender of q, not d; its schematic display has been corrected to q̵d. The TEI retains the conventional quod expansion and resolves the redundant nasal abbreviation as tantum.

Renewed inspection confirms crossing strokes at the second c in Siccar&, an added c above the baseline t in taticis, and marks beneath letters. The qualified deletion and substitution markup records these visible interventions without asserting their full sequence. The left marginal annotation remains partly legible as ta followed by uncertain joined strokes; the rest remains an illegible gap. Neither a complete marginal word nor a final reconstructed corrected verse is established. These are documented source uncertainties rather than a required editorial decision.
Que is retained as written; no unverified tail or diphthong is supplied. The final et sign completes habet in the TEI expansion.
The e in puella appears reworked and darker. Only that visible appearance is encoded; an earlier l or c cannot be securely established.

The source shows non blanda, a small supralinear e-like sign with an adjoining raised stroke, a lower insertion mark, and then non optima. The exact reading and any expansion of the raised sign remain uncertain. The low-certainty unclear addition and insertion mark are retained without supplying est or another conjectured expansion. This image limitation does not require a user to choose an unsupported reading.

Darker writing in adamantaque is visible on 63v. Earlier letters beneath it cannot be securely reconstructed from this image. The current word and the visible extent of darker ink are retained without a conjectured earlier state.
Small strokes distinguish the adjacent i letters in blanditiis. The second a in saxa is darker; the proposed underlying o is not securely legible and is not reconstructed.
The d in diuosque is legible in darker ink. Its predecessor cannot be established from the image and is not supplied.
The visible sequence supports nec uir ut ante fui. Word-division marks and darker ui are retained separately from the words.

The enlarged name supports phineius: an n-like pair of strokes follows phi, then ei. The witness form is retained rather than replaced by Phemius. The second u in iuuet is darker; the punctuation display remains schematic.
At que is retained with editorial segmentation of the visible sequence. No silent change of que to quae is made.

A horizontal nasal suspension above the i in fixi is visible and parallels the suspension used in qualē at 39. The transcription fīxi and TEI expansion finxi are retained. The separate lower-margin inscription is documented in its own note.
The final t in uigent is legible in darker ink. An earlier long s cannot be securely recovered and is not supplied.
The c in exposcunt is visibly darker. Miliciamque is retained as the source spelling; no correction to militiamque is imposed.

Supralinear vt is positioned over the underdotted es; the following et sign is also marked below. These visible interventions remain encoded separately. Their exact historical sequence or attribution to hands is not required to represent the visible page. Darker ti and tu are recorded separately.

Writing and surface across 73–74 are visibly disturbed. The visible text is retained; a proposed earlier skipped-line error and complete deleted verse cannot be securely reconstructed from this image.

Sollicitare manu is the visible current text. Faint traces beyond and beneath it cannot be read securely enough to assert per artes or reconstruct an earlier line. Their presence is documented here without conjectural deleted words.
The image supports corsurgere. This witness spelling is retained without automatic conversion to consurgere.
Fine word-division marks occur after me and quis. They are encoded separately from the words; the spacing is editorially segmented.
The first i in traiectis and fi in uenefica are darker. The image supports ramis; the familiar lanis is not substituted.
The image reads Deuouet aut alio lassus amore uenis. The corrected trial text is supported; the old example’s wording is not.
The final two couplets on 64r support the corrected 84-line ending. The first begins Nec mora desiluit tunica uelata soluta; the a of mora is darker.
The end of ministre is darker on a disturbed area. The visible spelling ministre is retained; an earlier state cannot be reconstructed securely.

Dots and a curved terminal stroke follow aqua before the next poem’s initial. The display :⌁ is schematic. Its location is certain but its checking or poem-end function is not, so the markup now uses unknown function.

The lower-right margin of 63v contains a short inscription with small marks above it, tentatively read si caret teum. The letters, abbreviation and relation to the poem remain uncertain. The inscription stays outside the verse sequence and unexpanded; this recorded limitation is not a request to invent a reading.
